Purpose                                   Tukuna a whakaaro auaha kia rere kia whakaumutia ai te ao.
      statement                                 Through creativity and innovation, we intervene to transform the world.



Technology is the study of how people use knowledge, resources, systems, and
processes to respond to needs, opportunities, and challenges. Students learn how
technological outcomes are designed, developed, evaluated, and improved, and how
they shape, and are shaped by, society and the environment.

Technology fosters curiosity about how things work, how they are made, and how
they can be improved. It develops creativity, innovation, precision, and judgement in
the design and development of technological outcomes. It empowers students to
apply knowledge, experiment with ideas, evaluate evidence, and see themselves as
capable contributors to the future.

Technology equips students with the knowledge, practices, and dispositions needed
to understand and influence their designed world as emerging technologists and
innovators. As students progress through Technology, they deepen their
understanding of how innovation and technological outcomes are enhanced through
interactions between people and cultures. Students learn how people identify
opportunities, respond to challenges, and create technological outcomes that
influence the lives of individuals, communities, and society.

The Technology learning area prepares students with the knowledge and practices to
access related curriculum subjects for Years 11–13.
